examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger, AccordionContent } from '@plexui/vue/components/Accordion';

const returnsDisabled = ref(false);
</script>

<template>
<Accordion type="single" collapsible default-value="shipping" style="width: 100%; max-width: 384px">
  <AccordionItem value="shipping">
    <AccordionTrigger>What are your shipping options?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>
      We offer standard (5–7 business days), express (2–3 days), and
      overnight shipping. Free standard shipping on orders over $50.
    </AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem value="returns" :disabled="returnsDisabled">
    <AccordionTrigger>What is your return policy?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>
      Returns are accepted within 30 days of delivery. Items must be unused
      and in original packaging. Refunds are processed within 5–7 business
      days of receipt.
    </AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem value="support">
    <AccordionTrigger>How can I contact customer support?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>
      Reach us by email, live chat, or phone Monday through Friday, 9am–6pm
      ET. Weekend tickets are handled within 24 hours.
    </AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
</template>
examples.details: Set type to multiple when readers can keep several sections open at once: settings pages, long FAQs, step-by-step references. A single accordion with collapsible lets readers close the open item; without it one item is always open. card composes the accordion inside Card, the most common landing-page FAQ pattern; on a phone the card is a section of the grouped list. The returnsDisabled control disables only the return-policy item. It remains visible and keeps its open state, while keyboard navigation skips its trigger.

components.name: Alert
components.description: Inline message for notices and warnings with semantic colors, variants, a title, a description, action slots, and a dismiss control.

props.name: title
props.description: Title displayed in the alert

props.name: description
props.description: Description text

props.name: actions
props.description: Actions (for example buttons)

props.name: actions-placement
props.description: Placement of actions; automatic from sizing when unset

props.name: mobile-actions
props.description: At 767px and below: 50px capsules as in an iOS tip, or the buttons at their own size, for an alert inside a block of its own buttons

props.name: actions-class-name
props.description: Class applied to the actions container

props.name: color
props.description: Color scheme

props.name: variant
props.description: Style variant

props.name: indicator
props.description: Custom indicator (slot), or :indicator="false" to hide it

props.name: @dismiss
props.description: Shows the dismiss button when set

props.name: banner
props.description: Full-width strip: square corners, lines above and below only

examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
<Alert
  :color="color"
  :variant="variant"
  :title="title ? 'Scheduled maintenance' : undefined"
  :description="description ? 'We\'ll be offline 2 - 4 AM UTC on July 14 while we upgrade our database.' : undefined"
  :indicator="indicator === 'none' ? false : undefined"
  :actions-placement="actionsPlacement === 'auto' ? undefined : actionsPlacement"
  :mobile-actions="mobileActions"
  :on-dismiss="onDismiss ? () => {} : undefined"
  :banner="banner"
>
  <template v-if="indicator === 'custom'" #indicator>
    <Lightbulb />
  </template>
  <template v-if="actions" #actions>
    <Button color="primary" variant="soft" pill>Set reminder</Button>
    <Button color="primary" variant="solid" pill>View status</Button>
  </template>
</Alert>
examples.details: color and variant style the alert. It shows a title, a description or both; each takes text, or content in the #title and #description slots, such as a <TextLink color="currentcolor"> to a status page. It has an indicator icon by default, chosen from its color: the indicator slot replaces it, and :indicator="false" hides it. The actions slot takes buttons or other content. They are placed automatically, at the end or, when they take more than a third of the alert's width, under the message, unless actions-placement is 'end' or 'bottom'. @dismiss adds a Dismiss button in the alert's chrome (this preview binds it as :on-dismiss, which can be left unset); for a dismissible notice, labeled buttons in actions are the suggested approach. A solid alert is for a message alone: buttons, Dismiss among them, do not read on its color, so this preview offers them on soft and outline alerts. Use banner for a full-width strip across the top or bottom of a page or panel (offline, read-only, a new version): it drops the rounded corners and keeps only the lines above and below. On a phone an alert takes the shape and text of an iOS tip (TipKit), the system's message inside a screen: 26px corners (a banner stays square), the title at 17/22 semibold and the description at 15/20, and a close button in its corner instead of Dismiss. A title or a description alone stands its first line on the middle of the icon. It keeps its icon, colors and variants, and its actions always stand under the message as 50px capsules side by side, so actions-placement is a desktop setting. With mobile-actions="own" the actions keep the size you give the buttons, for an alert inside a block of its own buttons.

components.description: An avatar for user identities that shows an initial, a photo or an icon, with overflow counts, semantic colors and roundness options.

props.description: Display name; used for text initial when no image/icon

props.name: image-url
props.description: Absolute URL for image avatar

props.name: Icon
props.description: Icon component for icon avatar, bound as :Icon

props.description: Width and height in pixels

props.name: color
props.description: Semantic color for text/icon avatar

props.name: variant
props.description: Style variant

props.name: overflow-count
props.description: Show overflow count (e.g. +9)

props.name: class
props.description: Applied to the avatar root

props.description: Makes avatar interactive (renders a button)

props.name: @pointerdown
props.description: Makes avatar interactive (renders a button)

examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
<Avatar
  :name="type === 'icon' ? 'Tech support' : type === 'overflow' ? overflowCount + ' more' : 'Tyler'"
  :image-url="type === 'image' ? 'https://gravatar.com/avatar/9531b260b9693f3394bea8646c6ea141ce58fe5a138b7db7729d60a4c5dde552' : undefined"
  :Icon="type === 'icon' ? Robot : undefined"
  :overflow-count="type === 'overflow' ? overflowCount : undefined"
  :size="size"
  :color="color"
  :variant="variant"
  :class="{ full: 'rounded-full', xl: 'rounded-xl', lg: 'rounded-lg', md: 'rounded-md', sm: 'rounded-sm', none: 'rounded-none' }[roundness]"
  v-on="onClick ? { click: saySup } : {}"
/>
examples.details: An avatar shows one of four things. Without other props it shows the first letter of name. With image-url, an absolute URL, it shows the photo with a soft fade once it loads, and the initial if it fails. With Icon, an icon component such as Robot from @plexui/vue/components/Icon, it shows the icon; name is not shown, and only names the avatar when it is a button. With overflow-count it shows the count, formatted and scaled to fit. size sets the width and height in pixels, and the initial, icon and count scale with it. color and variant style every avatar except a loaded photo, which covers them. Avatars are fully rounded by default; a Tailwind rounding class in class overrides that. Listening to @click (or @pointerdown) makes the avatar a button with interaction styles and its name as the accessible name.

props.name: color
props.description: Semantic color

props.description: Badge size

examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';

const color = ref("info"); // "secondary", "success", "warning", "danger", "info", "discovery", "caution"
const variant = ref("soft"); // or "solid", "outline"
const size = ref("md"); // "sm" to "xl"
const pill = ref(false);
const leading = ref("none"); // or "icon", "loading"
const onRemove = ref(false);
const shown = ref(true);
const labels = { none: "New", icon: "Beta", loading: "In progress" };
</script>

<template>
<Badge
  v-if="shown"
  :color="color"
  :variant="variant"
  :size="size"
  :pill="pill"
  :class="leading === 'loading' ? 'gap-1.5' : undefined"
  :remove-label="'Remove ' + labels[leading]"
  :on-remove="onRemove ? () => (shown = false) : undefined"
>
  <Flask v-if="leading === 'icon'" />
  <LoadingIndicator v-if="leading === 'loading'" />
  {{ labels[leading] }}
</Badge>
<Button v-else color="secondary" variant="outline" size="sm" @click="shown = true">Show again</Button>
</template>
examples.details: Style a badge with color and variant, and set its size; pill rounds it fully and adds horizontal gutter. Its content can be composed: an icon before the text takes the badge's color, size and spacing, and a LoadingIndicator marks a task in progress, with a wider gap-1.5 gap. @remove adds a cross at the end, with its own hover and focus, named by remove-label. To add the cross only at times, bind the handler as :on-remove and give it undefined otherwise, as here: Vue wraps an inline @remove expression in a function, so a listener written that way is always there. At size="xl" a badge has the height of a control, for a row of removable badges beside a button. Long text ends in an ellipsis and the cross stays.

examples.name: Overview
examples.details: A showcase of Button's key styles: solid, soft, outline, ghost, and icon-only. On a phone the example is a screen's actions as iOS 26 sets them: large buttons as wide as the screen, 11px apart, solid, soft and ghost. They stand at the top of the screen, next to the example's controls.

examples.name: Colors & variants
examples.code: {{ variant }}
examples.details: You can stylize the display of the button using the color and variant props. On a phone each variant is a screen's action in the two colors of iOS buttons, accent (primary) and destructive (danger): iOS draws solid as Filled, soft as Tinted or Gray and ghost as Plain; outline is Plex UI's own.

examples.name: Sizing & roundness
examples.code: {{ phoneSize.name }} · {{ phoneSize.size }} · {{ phoneSize.height }}px
examples.details: Control height with size and horizontal padding with gutter-size. Use pill for fully rounded corners. size sets the button to a specific control height, and gutter-size sets the horizontal padding. Each size provides default values for gutter-size and icon-size props, as well as font-size. Each of these values can be overridden independently. When pill is set, extra horizontal gutter is dynamically applied to the button. On a phone with touch.css a button takes one of the three heights of iOS buttons: small 28 (3xs to sm), medium 34 (md, lg) and large 50 (xl to 3xl), always a capsule: the small one with a 15px label and 10px gutters, the medium and large ones with a 17px label and 12 and 20px gutters, as iOS 27.2 sets them. Without size a button is md, the medium one; a screen's actions take xl. The Phone example shows the three as the kit's Button - Content Area does: a symbol with a label, a label alone, and a symbol alone, a circle. The label is Semibold, and Regular on a ghost button, as on iOS 26 screens.

examples.name: Icons
examples.code: {{ phoneSize.size }} · {{ phoneSize.height }}px
examples.details: Add icons to the default slot. Sizing is automatic via the icon-size prop. Default values for icon-size are provided through the size prop, but you can pass the prop directly to change the defaults. For icon-only buttons, there are two common approaches: Square: create perfect square icon buttons with the uniform prop. When uniform is passed, gutter-size is ignored. Combine with pill to make circular icons. Tighter gutters: on a desktop, applying a smaller gutter-size than size can create well-sized, but not exactly square, icon buttons. On a phone with touch.css the icon follows the three iOS sizes unless icon-size is set: 3xs to sm show the 18px icon and md to 3xl the 20px one, as iOS sets a button's symbol at the size of its label (15 and 17px). An icon-only button is the kit's symbol button, a circle as tall as a text button of its size, 28, 34 or 50px, with or without uniform, and gutter-size does not change it. A toolbar, the bars of Page and Dialog, a ButtonGroup of uniform buttons alone and a button beside a field keep the 44px circle of a bar button in the kit (50px at 3xl). Between an icon and a label a button leaves 8px at every size, as iOS 27.2 does; a loading button shows the iOS spinner, 18px in the small button and 20px in the medium and large ones.

examples.name: Block
examples.details: Create full-width buttons with the block prop. On a phone a screen's main action is the large button as wide as the screen (xl, 50px).

examples.details: Use optically-align with either "start" or "end" to offset the gutter of the button. On a phone a button under text starts its label where the text does, as Forgot your password? under the Apple Account sign-in, whose text starts 40px from the screen's edge; a soft button shows its capsule reaching past the text. The button is as wide as its label: a full-width button centers its label, which leaves nothing to align.

components.description: Join buttons into a single visual unit for toolbars, steppers, split buttons and search affordances.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Direction of the joined items

props.name: mobile-material
props.description: Phone surface with touch.css: "glass" makes the group one glass capsule outside a Toolbar, "flat" keeps the joined buttons in one

props.name: class
props.description: Applied to the root <div>

examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
Weekend trip

…
examples.details: Set size on every Button inside the group so corner radii match; the size setting here sets all of them. Mix icon-only (uniform) with text buttons; each child keeps its own padding. On a phone with touch.css a group in the content keeps one height. Beside text buttons its icon-only buttons take the heights of the iOS small (28px, sm) and medium (34px, md and lg) buttons; a group of icon-only buttons keeps their 44px, and beside a text field or a select every button takes the field's 44px. Joined segments have no iOS control of their own. On a phone the example is the bars of a note, as in iOS Notes: Back alone, the note's actions in one glass capsule on top, the editing tools in one at the bottom beside New Note. A ButtonGroup in a Toolbar is that capsule, as iOS 27.2 sets it: 44px buttons 10px apart in a 154px capsule on top, 48px ones 8px apart in a 164px capsule at the bottom, the symbols in the primary label color. Groups side by side stand apart as the bar's items do. The bar sets its buttons' size, so the phone view leaves out the size control.

examples.name: Orientation
examples.code:
<!-- Desktop -->
<ButtonGroup orientation="vertical" aria-label="Zoom controls">
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" :size="size" uniform aria-label="Zoom in">
    <PlusSm />
  </Button>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" :size="size" uniform aria-label="Zoom out">
    <Minus />
  </Button>
</ButtonGroup>

<!-- Phone: zoom controls over a canvas -->
<ButtonGroup orientation="vertical" mobile-material="glass" aria-label="Zoom controls" class="absolute top-2 right-4">
  <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="Zoom in"><Plus /></Button>
  <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="Zoom out"><Minus /></Button>
</ButtonGroup>

examples.name: Overview
examples.details: A checkbox is checked, unchecked or indeterminate. Pass checked="indeterminate", or default-checked="indeterminate", for a partly selected state: a "select all" box whose items are only partly checked, as in Group with select all. solid (default) fills the box; ghost renders only the checkmark, in the text color, without a border or background, for subtle inline selections or task lists. pill rounds the box (border-radius: full): the solid fill, and on a ghost box its hover tint and focus ring. Use description (or the description slot) for a second line under the label. It sits outside the label, so the checkbox keeps the label as its name and gets the description through aria-describedby. By default the box is on the left of its label; orientation="right" places it after the label. Both act only next to a label, so they are offered only with one. Without a label the checkbox is a standalone control: pass aria-label to name it. disabled keeps the checked and indeterminate states. On a phone with touch.css a solid checkbox is the 22px selection circle of iOS with or without pill, so the phone view has no pill setting. A ghost checkbox is the checkmark of an iOS list row.

examples.name: Overview
examples.details: On a phone a dialog is one of the two modal views of iOS: an Alert (mobile-variant="alert"), a short question with its answers, or a Sheet, which it is by default (see Placement). The main action is preferred (solid: the accent fill on a phone), plain (soft), or destructive (color="danger": a red label on the alert's fill on a phone). A title without a message stands centered. examples.details: An empty message is made of parts, each optional: an icon, a title, a description and an action row. It needs a title or a description, so this preview offers description with a title; the description takes text or nodes, such as a search term in font-semibold. color on EmptyMessageIcon and on EmptyMessageTitle shows the intent of the message, such as danger on both for an error (a missing permission) or warning on the icon for a notice (a feature in beta); the description keeps its own color. fill sizes the message to its parent: static takes the full width and height, absolute covers a positioned parent, and none applies no sizing, for a container that sets the height (a list with no results). The action row takes buttons, or a TextLink with class="text-sm" on the row. On a phone a message of the default size takes the shape of the kit's empty state: the symbol in a 64px slot, a 22px bold title over a 17px description, and its buttons 24px under the text, one at its own width and two across the width one under the other. The layout control puts the label in its four places: above: the default, orientation="vertical". columns: orientation="horizontal", every value starting at one column. end: row, one line of a FieldGroup with the value at its end. A framed field is a pill there and takes --field-row-control-width, as its width cannot follow what is typed; :pill="false" on the control keeps the rounded box. hidden: hide-label. The label still names the control for screen readers; the placeholder shows what to type, and a description moves under the field. On Phone a field is always a cell of a FieldGroup on the grouped background, as in an iOS form, in the same four places: the label above its value (row orientation="vertical"), values in one column (FieldGroup columns), the value at the end of the row, or the placeholder alone (row hide-label), its value starting at the row's edge. The row is the field's frame, so a framed or soft field loses its frame. The error stands inside the cell, under the value. The words that explain a field go in the group's footer slot, and a required field says so in its placeholder, as iOS account forms do. A disabled field dims its label with its value. A one-time code is the exception: OTPInput keeps its own digit cells on the screen, outside a group, as in Verify email.

Its title names the group, description stands under the title, the action slot at the end of the header, and the footer slot under the rows; paragraphs of a footer stand apart. columns starts every value at one column, --field-row-column-width into the row. header-prominence="increased" makes the title lead its content, as a section of a page. On Phone the standard title is the quiet heading of an iOS list, and the increased one is the list's prominent header, 20pt Semibold in the primary label. A ghost text button in the header is the list header's action: tinted text on the title's last line, with a 44pt target. The footer is 13/16 Footnote, its paragraphs one empty line apart, as in Settings.

examples.name: Other controls
examples.details: Field works with any form control. A native one, such as a Textarea, is named by the label's for. A Select or DatePicker trigger is not a native form control, so Field points its aria-labelledby at the label, and the trigger adds its value: a screen reader hears "Role, Editor". A child with a name of its own (aria-label, aria-labelledby or label) keeps it. On Phone a Select or a date is the value at the end of its row, and a long text stands under its label. A group of checkboxes, radios or switches is a row per choice: see Checkbox, Radio Group and Switch.

components.name: Float Input
components.description: Text input whose label floats above the value, with error and helper text, a clear button, a password reveal toggle, and a multi-line variant.

examples.name: Overview
examples.details: Two things set the type: where the label rests (label-placement: on the border, or inside the box with the value under it), and the shape of the field. An empty field shows the label as a placeholder, so the difference appears once it has a value or the focus. :pill="false" takes the rounded box of Input and Select with the label on the border; inside always takes the rounded box, so pill is offered only with the label on the border. Text fields, textareas and selects take both settings the same way. Both floating fields follow the same two tokens, so a form can set its radius and gutter in one place. Choose Empty or Filled to replace the value with a preset. The other controls preserve your text. Invalid and errorMessage demonstrate visual states, not email validation. An error message also marks the field invalid, so invalid is offered only without one; when both messages are enabled, the error appears before the description. Read-only text can still be selected and copied. onClear shows a built-in clear button: it appears when the field has a value and is not disabled or read-only, and focus returns to the field. Listen to @clear, or bind :on-clear as here to switch it on and off. On Phone the field is a cell named by its placeholder: the label does not float and the cell is the frame, so label-placement and pill are desktop settings. The description goes in the group's footer and the error stands inside the cell. A cell has no frame to color, so invalid alone is desktop only.

examples.details: indicator picks one of the three. LoadingIndicator is a spinner for general loading states. It takes the surrounding font-size and text color by default; size and stroke-width set its size and stroke in pixels, a text class such as text-danger (or --indicator-color) colors it, and --indicator-rotate-duration sets the time of one turn. On a desktop it is a turning ring. With the optional touch stylesheet it is the iOS 27 spinner of eight rounded spokes: 20px by default, also inside a field (an Input adornment, an InputGroup addon or a SelectControl, through --control-indicator-size); up to 16px it takes the Small spokes and from 28px the Large ones. A stroke-width replaces the spokes' widths, so the Phone view leaves it unset. CircularProgress is a progress ring. Without progress it simulates progress over max-duration milliseconds, and done fills the ring and ends the simulation; this preview sets it every 4 seconds to start over. progress, from 0 to 100, shows a fixed value instead. size and stroke-width (at most 4) size the ring, and track-color and track-active-color color its track and its progress. LoadingDots shows typing progress with staggered pulsing dots in the current text color.

Variants

The state control shows each variant empty, with a value, invalid and disabled. You decide how the invalid state is removed, whether that's through @focus, @update:value, a submit handler, etc.; [data-invalid] is applied to the container for custom styling. disabled greys the input out and prevents user interactions. On Phone the row is the frame, and the value stands in one of three places: at the end of the row, at one column for the whole group with FieldGroup columns, or under the label with orientation="vertical". A row has no frame to color, so an error is the row's error-message under it.

examples.name: Adornments

Ideally, the spacing will look pretty good by default. If you need to customize the spacing: gutter-size determines the amount of spacing on the edges of the container, which you can fine-tune as needed (if you need precise spacing not supported by gutter-size, use a negative margin on your adornment directly, e.g. -ml-2). The spacing between the adornment and the input is controlled with gap on the container, which you can customize as needed with Tailwind classes. On Phone an Input in a Toolbar takes the bar's search field, and one with type="search" at the top of the content is the flat search field under a large title; in a row a start adornment is a prefix of the value, such as a currency, and trailing text-secondary text takes the row's accessory color.

examples.details: The header has no line at rest. Scroll the content: the line comes after 4px and goes again at the top. Turn divider off to keep the header without it. A page with fill does not scroll under its header, so on desktop the line does not come and the divider is offered without fill; on a phone only a glass or hard header draws the line, so there the divider is offered with those. width belongs to the page, so the line, the title, the buttons and the content always stand in one column. Take full for tables, wide for overviews and column for settings and forms; for any other width set --page-width on the page. This frame is narrower than a screen, so the preview shows both widths at half their size. fill stops the page scrolling from 768px up, so a table can scroll inside itself. On a phone a page takes the width of the screen at every width and scrolls as a whole, so the phone has neither setting. PageHeading groups the title with metadata in PageSubtitle. On a phone the badge and subtitle share a second row below the centered title. The header grows when metadata wraps, and the content keeps the corresponding space below it. PageLeading holds a Back button or the menu button of a sidebar, before the title; on a phone the title stays centred between it and the actions. On a phone background sets how the header and the footer meet the content scrolled under them, as a Toolbar does: glass, the header's default, is a translucent, blurred bar with a hairline, soft, the footer's default, fades the canvas color out under a header and leaves the content clear under the footer's actions, as native iOS 26 does, hard is an opaque bar with a line, and solid an opaque bar with no line. Glass and hard show themselves once content is under the bar. surface="grouped" gives the phone canvas the gray of grouped rows; desktop colors stay. The footer and its background stand under the preview, as what sits at the bottom of the screen.

examples.details: SegmentedControl provides two visual variants: segmented (default) with a sliding background highlight, and underline with an animated line indicator under the active tab and no background container. Bind the selected tab with v-model:value; the examples keep it in a tab variable. flush makes the underline indicator match the text width exactly, with gap between tabs instead of padding, and block stretches the tabs evenly across the container. orientation="vertical" stacks the tabs: the thumb slides up and down, and the underline becomes a line on the left side, for sidebar-style navigation. Both variants take the full 9-step size scale of Button, Input, Select and SelectControl, which sets the height, font size, icon size and spacing of the tabs. Put an icon in a tab's icon slot, or pass a component to its icon prop, to show it before the label, sized to the size; leave out the label for icon-only tabs of a horizontal control and give each an aria-label. Vertical tabs keep their labels, so the example offers no icon only there: they are a list, a sidebar or on a phone an inset grouped list, and a list row always has a title. badge takes a number or an object with content, color, variant and pill, shown after the label inside the control; a count names what it counts, so it sits on a labelled tab and icon-only tabs carry none. disabled affects the whole group, which on a phone shows at half opacity when horizontal, as a disabled iOS segmented control does; monthDisabled disables only Month, whose label in a horizontal control on a phone takes the disabled label of iOS, 20% of the label color, while its row in a vertical one shows at half opacity. Arrow-key navigation skips disabled tabs without resetting the selected value.On a phone horizontal tabs of either variant are the iOS 27 segmented control, filling the row of a phone screen, in its two sizes. The default md and larger are the large control of iOS 27 apps, as Calendar and Reminders draw it and SwiftUI draws a segmented Picker in a toolbar: a 48px glass capsule, a 40px gray selection 4px inside it, 8px between segments, every label 15px Medium and primary. sm and smaller are the small one, the plain control of SwiftUI's Picker in content and of Safari's bookmarks: a 32px capsule of the tertiary fill, a white selection 2px inside it, labels 13px, Semibold when selected. mobileMaterial switches the look, as for Button: flat makes the large one plain, 49px as SwiftUI's .controlSize(.large), and glass puts the small one under the Liquid Glass of .glassEffect(). Inside a phone Toolbar every control is the large glass one. The phone example puts the control in a top bar between Close and Confirm, as a sheet's toolbar holds a segmented Picker in iOS 27.2 and Calendar its new event, in a bottom bar, or above the content, as Safari's bookmarks do, over a day that scrolls under the glass of the bars; placement picks one. Vertical tabs of either variant are an inset grouped list, as iOS lists a choice: 52px rows with the 17px label and a checkmark on the selected row instead of the thumb. A segment with an icon and a label shows the icon alone, at the 20px symbol size, as UISegmentedControl draws an action with a title and an image; the label stays the segment's accessible name, since iOS segments carry a title or a symbol, not both. They carry no badges either: on a phone write a count into the label instead, or leave it out. Underline tabs draw the same segmented control on a phone and every control there is a capsule filling its row, so the phone view has no variant, flush, block, pill and badge controls, and its size offers sm and md.

Without block the trigger fits its value and the list is at least list-min-width, here 240px, wider than the trigger, so align places it against the trigger. side is the side the list prefers. check-position puts the checkmark at the start or the end of a row; "none" leaves the column out. clearable adds a clear action. loading shows loading-placeholder and keeps the list closed. disabled disables the select, and a disabled select is not submitted with its form. optically-align offsets the trigger by its gutter: "start" puts the text of a ghost trigger on the label's edge, and "end" puts the end of a block one, its indicator, on the field's end.     <ToolbarTitle>Home</ToolbarTitle>
  </Toolbar>
  <PageContent>...</PageContent>
  <TabBar
    v-model:value="tab"
    :search="{ value: 'search' }"
    :prominent="{ value: 'bag', label: 'Bag' }"
    minimize-behavior="onScrollDown"
    background="soft"
  >

    </TabBarItem>

    </TabBarItem>

examples.details: Put the bar last in a Page: it reserves its height there. Up to three tabs sit in the middle, 85px apart, as iOS 27 sets them; four and five share the width. The selected tab sits on a pill in the primary text, the others in a lighter gray, as Sidebar items are. With search the search tab takes a glass circle of its own at the trailing end, as the iOS 26 search tab does, and the capsule keeps to the leading end at the width of its tabs; show the search screen when its value is selected. With prominent one key destination, such as a cart or a library, takes that circle instead, as the prominent tab of iOS 27: it is still a tab, the circle shows the symbol from the prominent-icon slot only and label names it, and with both the search tab joins the capsule as its last tab. The bar holds five tabs at most, the search and prominent tabs counted, as in the kit's Tab Bar - iPhone: next to a circle the capsule keeps four, so the example disables the counts that would not fit. With minimize-behavior="onScrollDown" the bar shrinks while the content scrolls down to a circle of the selected tab at the leading end, the search or prominent circle staying at the trailing end, as the minimized tab bar of the kit; it comes back when the content scrolls up, and a tap on the minimized tab brings the others back. A tab's badge shows a count or a short word in a red capsule over its symbol, as an iOS tab badge, and the minimized circle keeps it; a count of 0 shows none. The accessory slot puts the app's own content, a now playing row or a status, in a glass capsule above the tabs, as the bottom accessory of iOS 27: minimized, it moves between the two circles, and the bar keeps its height so the content does not move. background sets how the bar meets the content scrolled under it, as on a Toolbar: soft (the default) leaves the content clear around the capsule, as native iOS 26 does, glass lays a translucent, blurred band with a hairline under it, hard an opaque band with a line on top and solid an opaque band with no line. examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { compact as compactOptions, toast } from '@plexui/vue/components/Toast';

const type = ref("default"); // or "success", "error", "warning", "info"
const icon = ref(true); // the type's icon; false passes icon: null
const description = ref("none"); // or "short", "long"
const action = ref("none"); // or "action", "cancel" (an action and a cancel)
const closeButton = ref(false);
const compact = ref(false);
const persistent = ref(false); // with an action or a close button

// Each type's title, its short description and its action's label
const messages = {
  default: { title: "Changes saved", description: "Your profile is live for everyone on the team.", action: "Undo" },
  success: { title: "Inquiry ID copied", description: "Paste it into the support form.", action: "Open" },
  error: { title: "Failed to assign owner", description: "The owner has left the workspace.", action: "Retry" },
  warning: { title: "Session expires in 2 minutes", description: "Unsaved changes will be lost.", action: "Stay" },
  info: { title: "New version available", description: "Reload to get the latest features.", action: "Reload" },
};
const longDescription = "This is a long message to show how the toast handles multi-line content without clipping or awkward wrapping. The title and description should both wrap cleanly.";
</script>

<template>
<Button
  color="secondary"
  variant="outline"
  @click="(type === 'default' ? toast : toast[type])(messages[type].title, {
    icon: icon ? undefined : null,
    description: description === 'none' ? undefined : description === 'short' ? messages[type].description : longDescription,
    action: action === 'none' ? undefined : { label: messages[type].action, onClick: () => {} },
    cancel: action === 'cancel' ? { label: 'Cancel', onClick: () => {} } : undefined,
    closeButton,
    duration: persistent && (action !== 'none' || closeButton) ? Infinity : undefined,
    ...(compact ? compactOptions : {}),
  })"
>
  Show toast
</Button>
</template>
examples.details: Call toast with a message, or toast.success, .error, .warning and .info for the semantic types, which map to PlexUI's success, danger, warning and info tokens. Each of them shows its icon; icon: null leaves it out, and icon takes a component of your own instead. No richColors is passed, so the types retheme with data-theme. The options add a description under the message, an action button and a cancel one (either closes the toast after its onClick), and closeButton. Spread compact into the options for a centered toast: on a desktop a toast shrinks to its content anyway, and on a phone, where a toast fills the width, a compact one keeps the width of its content. duration: Infinity keeps a toast open until the user closes it, so give it a labelled action or a close button: a way to close it from the keyboard. An error that waits like this is an alert (see Screen readers). On a phone a toast takes the corners, padding and text of an iOS notification banner, the system's own message at the top of the screen: 24px corners and 15pt text, with its buttons drawn as a medium phone Button, a 34px capsule in a 44px target. One button stands at the end of the message's row, where a banner shows its time, and the message wraps in its own column; a cancel and an action together stand under the message, and so does a button that would leave the message less than half the row (8em in a toast as wide as its content). Under 600px it fills the width between 14px gutters past the safe area, as notifications do on an iOS phone; a compact toast keeps its own width. It stays a message of the page, with an opaque surface.

examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { Button, NavigationButton } from '@plexui/vue/components/Button';
import { DotsHorizontal, Filter, Plus, PlusLg, Search, SearchSm, Translate } from '@plexui/vue/components/Icon';
import { Input } from '@plexui/vue/components/Input';
import { Page, PageContent } from '@plexui/vue/components/Page';
import { Toolbar, ToolbarContent, ToolbarGroup, ToolbarLeading, ToolbarTitle, ToolbarTrailing } from '@plexui/vue/components/Toolbar';

const search = ref(false); // a search field in place of the title
const title = ref(true); // false: the bar holds its controls alone
const titleStyle = ref<"inline" | "large" | "compact-large" | "compact-medium">("inline");
const titleAlign = ref<"center" | "start">("center"); // an inline title only
const subtitle = ref(false); // not with a compact title
const group = ref(false);
const topBackground = ref<"soft" | "hard" | "glass" | "solid">("glass");
const bottom = ref<"none" | "buttons" | "search" | "action">("none"); // "search": one search field to a screen
const bottomBackground = ref<"soft" | "hard" | "glass" | "solid">("soft");
</script>

<template>
<Page surface="grouped">
  <Toolbar :title-style="!search && title ? titleStyle : ..." :title-align="!search && title && titleStyle === 'inline' ? titleAlign : undefined" :background="topBackground">
    <ToolbarContent v-if="search" fill>
      <Input variant="soft" pill placeholder="Search" aria-label="Search orders">
        <template #startAdornment>
          <SearchSm />
        </template>
      </Input>
    </ToolbarContent>
    <ToolbarLeading v-if="!search && !(title && titleStyle.startsWith('compact'))">
      <NavigationButton action="back" />
    </ToolbarLeading>
    <ToolbarTitle v-if="!search && title" :subtitle="subtitle && !titleStyle.startsWith('compact') ? '24 orders' : undefined">Orders</ToolbarTitle>
    <ToolbarTrailing>
      <NavigationButton v-if="search" action="close" aria-label="Close search" />
      <ToolbarGroup v-else-if="group" aria-label="Order actions">
        <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="Translate"><Translate /></Button>
        <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="More"><DotsHorizontal /></Button>
      </ToolbarGroup>
      <NavigationButton v-else :action="title && titleStyle === 'large' ? 'confirm' : 'close'" />
    </ToolbarTrailing>
  </Toolbar>
  <PageContent>
    undefined
  </PageContent>
  <Toolbar v-if="bottom !== 'none' && !(search && bottom === 'search')" placement="bottom" :background="bottomBackground">
    <template v-if="bottom === 'buttons'">
      <ToolbarLeading>
        <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="Filter"><Filter /></Button>
      </ToolbarLeading>
      <ToolbarContent>
        <Button color="primary" pill>New order</Button>
      </ToolbarContent>
      <ToolbarTrailing v-if="!search">
        <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="Search"><Search /></Button>
      </ToolbarTrailing>
    </template>
    <template v-else-if="bottom === 'search'">
      <ToolbarContent fill>
        <Input variant="soft" pill placeholder="Search" aria-label="Search orders">
          <template #startAdornment>
            <SearchSm />
          </template>
        </Input>
      </ToolbarContent>
      <ToolbarTrailing>
        <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill icon-size="sm" aria-label="New order"><PlusLg /></Button>
      </ToolbarTrailing>
    </template>
    <ToolbarContent v-else fill>
      <Button color="primary" pill block><Plus /> New order</Button>
    </ToolbarContent>
  </Toolbar>
</Page>
</template>
examples.details: Leading and trailing items take 44px targets; an inline title is centered across the whole width. title-style sets the size and place of the title: inline in the row of controls, large on a row of its own below them (on a page it scrolls up with the content under the controls, which then show it inline), and compact-large or compact-medium at the leading edge of the row, on a screen with no Back button. subtitle adds a second line under an inline or large title. title-align="start" puts an inline title after the leading items. Scroll the content: the canvas color fades out over the rows under the bar, and the glass starts to cast a shadow. ToolbarGroup puts related actions in one capsule; a single action, as Back or Close, keeps a capsule of its own. Without ToolbarTitle the bar holds its controls alone. A ButtonGroup in a toolbar is the same capsule. Name each icon button with aria-label. ToolbarContent fill stretches a search field across the row in the place of the title, up to the trailing items; the field takes the row height and the material of the bar buttons. placement="bottom" sets the bar at the bottom of the page with 48px targets and the device's bottom safe area. ToolbarContent centers a main action; with fill a search field or a single action takes the whole row. The 48px items stand 28px from the sides and above the home indicator, 12px apart, and a bottom bar draws no band: the content runs under and around its glass, as in iOS 26 Mail and Contacts. On a band (glass, hard or solid) a page's bottom bar is the top bar turned over: 10px above its items, its side items at the bar's gutter (16px, 20px from 414px), where the top bar's corner items and a grouped list's rows stand, and that gutter or the home indicator's inset less 6px under them. A search field holds SearchSm, set in Regular; a plus next to it takes icon-size="sm", as Contacts draws it smaller than the other symbols. The page content scrolls under both bars. A screen holds one search field, so with one in the top bar the bottom bar offers neither its own field nor its Search button. background sets how a bar meets the content scrolled under it. glass, the default of a top bar, is a translucent, blurred bar with a hairline. soft, the default of a bottom bar, is the scroll edge effect of iOS 26 and draws no line: a top bar with a title covers the content under its controls with the canvas color and fades it out past them over a light blur, while a top bar of controls alone on a page covers only the status bar, and a bottom bar on a page leaves the content clear under and around its controls, as native iOS 26 does (Contacts, Notes, Mail); each glass control stands out by itself. A Sheet's bottom bar fades its content into the panel. hard is an opaque bar of the canvas color with a line. solid is an opaque bar with no line. Glass and hard show themselves once content is under the bar: under the top bar after the content has scrolled, over the bottom bar while it continues below. PageHeader, PageFooter, the bars of a Sheet and TabBar take the same values. The top and the bottom bar each take their own; the bottom bar's controls stand under the preview.
